claims.value: Welden’s Austrian table distinguishes marching-out strength 137,542 (122,190 infantry and 15,352 cavalry) from fighting/firearms strength 118,322 (105,635 and 12,669).
claims.rationale: Table headings: Ausrückender Stand, all ranks, versus Streitbarer Stand, firearms; campaign/battle-date compiled table, not all actually engaged. Printed infantry fighting total plus cavalry equals 118,304, eighteen below the printed 118,322; retain the printed total and arithmetic discrepancy. English rendering (ours): "Total: 122,190; 15,352; 137,542; 105,635; 12,669; 118,322."

citations.locator: welden, printed p. 157, Internet Archive leaf 181; inspected page-image excerpt

claims.value: Welden deducts 7,744 detached fifth-corps troops from the printed 118,322 to obtain 110,578 Austrian fighting strength.
claims.rationale: Source’s deduction, not a new inferred opening estimate; comparison differs from Bodart’s 130,000 available. English rendering (ours): "We therefore obtain 110,578 men as the fighting strength of the Austrians."

citations.locator: welden, printed p. 157, Internet Archive leaf 181; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Wir erhalten sonach 110.578 Mann als den streitbaren Stand der Oesterreicher.

claims.value: Welden compares his Austrian fighting total with 172,552 French after deducting detachments and Extracorps, versus Bodart’s 160,000 available.
claims.rationale: Austrian author’s mediated French comparison; no averaging or preference by national reputation. English rendering (ours): "That of the French, after deduction of all detachments and Extracorps, amounting to 172,552 men."
